subject.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove

question: Should OpenClaw core adopt the experimental one-Claw/one-agent status/remove lifecycle with its proposed orphan recovery, retained referenced-resource defaults, and no permanent removal tombstone?
rationale: This is a new core lifecycle and deletion contract affecting agent config, workspaces, sessions, and package ownership; code review cannot choose the intended operator-recovery semantics or core-versus-extension scope.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded experimental contract
options.body: Keep the feature behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`, require the missing real cleanup proof, and merge it only with the preceding package-lifecycle stack.

options.title: Require a stronger recovery design first
options.body: Pause this slice until maintainers specify whether completed removals need durable operator-visible recovery history or a Doctor-owned reconciliation path.

options.title: Keep lifecycle orchestration outside core
options.body: Decline the core direction and retain existing agent/package owner commands as the supported lifecycle surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded experimental contract
recommendation.body: Keep the feature behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`, require the missing real cleanup proof, and merge it only with the preceding package-lifecycle stack.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comment identifies the unresolved lifecycle authority and recovery semantics directly.
